chronology.event: Begins photographing and electronically recording anomalous activity over the Manzano Weapons Storage Area, Kirtland AFB.
AFOSI document records Kirtland security police observations of unexplained aerial objects over Coyote Canyon and notes Bennewitz's activity.
Begins receiving material from AFOSI-connected sources describing alleged underground alien facilities.
Hospitalised for psychiatric care; withdraws from the field.

claims.text: On American Alchemy with Jesse Michels, 5 July 2025, at 0:36:14, Greg Bishop said that Doty told him, and he thinks Moore told him, that the Air Force flew Bennewitz by helicopter from Kirtland to Archuleta Mesa on the Jicarilla Apache reservation and showed him a site, and that jeeps, water tanks 'and all kind of stuff' had been placed there as props so his attention would move away from Kirtland. At 0:37:25 he said something did later crash there, that Bennewitz reached the site only after it had been cleaned up, and that what was found was burned ground, broken brush and a pen marked US government property. Nothing in the board's files mentions Archuleta.

claims.source: American Alchemy with Jesse Michels, 'Fake Alien Signals Drove Him Insane... (ft. Greg Bishop)', 5 July 2025, 0:34:30
claims.text: At 0:34:30 in the same episode Bishop said that in his own reading Bennewitz 'was his own worst enemy' and that the specific thing he knows Bill Moore did was to be told to give Bennewitz the Aquarius document, in which two of Bennewitz's own films are mentioned. The author of the standard account is on the record limiting what he says was actually done to the man.

THE BURIAL RECORD, WHICH THE LITERATURE NEVER CARRIES. Paul Frederick Bennewitz Jr, 30 September 1927 to 23 June 2003, buried at Santa Fe National Cemetery, Santa Fe County, New Mexico, Section 12 Site 402, marker inscribed 'S1C US COAST GUARD WORLD WAR II'. The man at the centre of the best-documented domestic disinformation operation in this subject was a Second World War Coast Guard seaman who ran a humidity-instrument company.

claims.source: Stephen Fisher, The Trenchant Edges Newsletter, 29 November 2025, https://www.trenchantedges.com/p/what-did-they-do-to-paul-bennewitz , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: HIS OWN DATED DOCUMENT, WHICH THE BOARD HAS NOT CARRIED. Bennewitz summarised his own investigation in late 1981 in a roughly five-thousand-word report titled 'Project Beta: SUMMARY OF REPORT AND STATUS (WITH SUGGESTED GUIDELINES)'. Two fragments of it were read: 'IN TRUTH THEY TEND TO LIE, HOWEVER THEIR MEMORY FOR LYING IS NOT LONG' and 'THEY MUST BE MADE TO COME DOWN - DESTRUCT THEMSELVES WHICH IS A STANDING ORDER'. Tier 2 because the fragments were read in a 2025 newsletter and not in the document.

claims.text: INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION OF THE 1980 AFOSI RECORD. The complaint form reproduced by NICAP from the CUFON archive carries AFOSI Det 1700 at Kirtland AFB, District File No. 8017D93-0/29, and Richard C Doty, SA, on its face, together with named 1608 Security Police Squadron observers: SSGT Stephen Ferenz, area supervisor, ATC Martin W. Rist and AMN Anthony D. Frazier at approximately 2350 hrs on 8 August 1980, and an unnamed Sandia security guard at approximately 0020 hrs on 9 August 1980 who requested anonymity.

Bennewitz is the origin point of the Dulce claim, from about 1979, in the dated chronology of the cluster's originators. Myrna Hansen's 1980 abduction claim was connected to Dulce by Bennewitz after he had begun to suspect a facility there.

label: Paul Frederick Bennewitz
narrative: Bennewitz is the clearest documented casualty of a US counterintelligence operation run against an American civilian over UFO information. He was a working physicist who ran Thunder Scientific Corporation, an instrumentation firm whose customers included the Air Force, from a property whose sightlines took in the Manzano Weapons Storage Area and Coyote Canyon on the eastern edge of Kirtland AFB. From 1979 he recorded lights and electronic signals over the Manzano nuclear-weapons storage complex and reported them - to the Air Force, in writing, repeatedly. The Air Force's documented response was an AFOSI file: a formal AFOSI complaint-form record dated 10 November 1980 confirming that Kirtland security police had observed unexplained aerial objects over Coyote Canyon and that Bennewitz's photography and reporting were under official notice. What followed, on the accounts of the AFOSI personnel involved, was not an investigation but a feed: Bennewitz was supplied with fabricated material about underground alien bases, treaties and biological experiments, calibrated to his existing beliefs, in order to discredit him and to mask whatever it was he had actually recorded near a nuclear storage site. He deteriorated, was hospitalised for psychiatric care in 1988, and died in 2003. The Bennewitz affair is the template: the state does not need to seize a witness's evidence if it can destroy the witness's credibility, and it can do that using its own personnel, on the record, with no legal consequence.

timeline.label: Bennewitz becomes the origin point of the Dulce claim
timeline.text: From about 1979 Paul Bennewitz, an Albuquerque instrument manufacturer whose company overlooked the Manzano storage area, began the personally funded study that made him the first person to attach a facility claim to Dulce. He later connected Myrna Hansen's 1980 account to the same place.

timeline.label: Bennewitz hospitalised
timeline.text: After eight years of fabricated material fed to him through AFOSI channels, Paul Bennewitz is hospitalised for psychiatric care and withdraws from the field.
